Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Option<String>,\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    // Initialize logging\n    let level = match cli.log_level.as_str() {\n        \"trace\" => Level::TRACE,\n        \"debug\" => Level::DEBUG,\n        \"warn\" => Level::WARN,\n        \"error\" => Level::ERROR,\n        _ => Level::INFO,\n    };\n\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_max_level(level)\n        .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    // ── WireGuard Explicit --http/--ws/--grpc flags\n    // always win regardless of the WG interface state.\n    let run_stdio = cli.stdio\n        || cli.all\n        || (cli.http.is_none() && cli.sse.is_none() && cli.ws.is_none() && cli.grpc.is_none());\n    let all_ip = wg_ip.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"0.0.0.0\");\n    let http_addr = cli.http.or(cli.sse).or(if cli.all {\n        Some(format!(\"{all_ip}:3001\"))\n    } else {\n        None\n    });\n    let ws_addr = cli.ws.or(if cli.all {\n        Some(format!(\"{all_ip}:3002\"))\n    } else {\n        None\n    });\n    let grpc_addr = cli.grpc.or(if cli.all {\n        Some(format!(\"{all_ip}:50051\"))\n    } else {\n        None\n    });\n\n    // Create and run server based on mode\n    match mode {\n        ServerMode::Compact => {\n            let executor: Arc<dyn ToolExecutor> = Arc::new(LazyOpToolsExecutor);\n            let server = Arc::new(CompactServer::new(executor));\n            info!(\"Compact MCP server initialized with lazy op-tools registry\");\n\n            run_transports(\n                server,\n                run_stdio,\n                http_addr,\n                ws_addr,\n                grpc_addr,\n                Some(\"/mcp/compact\"),\n            )\n            .await\n        }\n\n        ServerMode::Full => {\n            let config = McpServerConfig {\n                name: cli.name,\n                compact_mode: false,\n                ..Default::default()\n            };\n\n            let server = McpServer::new(config).await?;\n            info!(mode = %mode, \"MCP server initialized\");\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f271f-f024-7830-9dd1-c38e0ce043ea"}}}

vector_id           [u8; 16]   offset 92   (Qdrant episode UUID)\n///   reserved            [u8; 44]   offset 108\n#[repr(C)]\npub struct IdentitySled {\n    /// Raw Curve25519 WireGuard peer key.\n    pub wireguard_pubkey: [u8; 32],\n    /// Monotonic schema mutation counter.\n    pub mutation_index: u64,\n    /// Blake3 hashed footprint of the canonicalized schema state.\n    pub hashed_footprint: [u8; 32],\n    /// UUID v4 trace ID (16 raw bytes, network order).\n    pub trace_id: [u8; 16],\n    /// Schema version for compatibility.\n    pub schema_version: u32,\n    /// Qdrant vector ID for the last reasoning episode (UUID v4, 16 raw bytes).\n    /// Bound to identity: every vectorized episode is traceable to this sled.\n    pub vector_id: [u8; 16],\n    /// Reserved for future use (zero-initialized).\n    pub reserved: [u8; 44],\n}\n\nimpl IdentitySled {\n    pub const SIZE: usize = std::mem::size_of::<Self>();\n\n    /// Hex-encode the trace_id field for header String {\n        hex::encode(self.vector_id)\n    }\n\n    /// UUID string representation of vector_id.\n    pub fn vector_id_uuid(&self) -> String {\n        let b = self.vector_id;\n        format!(\n            \"{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}-{:02x}{:02x}-{:02x}{:02x}-{:02x}{:02x}-{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}\",\n footprint and trace_id are non-zero.\n    pub fn is_sled_valid(&self) -> bool {\n        self.hashed_footprint != [0u8; 32] && self.trace_id != [0u8; 16]\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Zero-Btrfs disk-I/O guard Xray config writes must live in tmpfs.\nfn assert_tmpfs_or_abort(path: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let parent = std::path::Path::new(path)\n        .parent()\n {\n                name: tool.name,\n                description: tool.description,\n                input_schema: tool.input_schema,\n                annotations: None,\n            })\n            .collect())\n    }\n\n    async fn execute_tool(&self, name: &str, arguments: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        let registry = Self::load_registry().await?;\n        let tool = registry\n            .get(name)\n            .await\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Tool not found: {}\", name))?;\n        tool.execute(arguments).await\n    }\n\n    async fn get_tool_schema(&self, name: definition.input_schema))\n    }\n\n    async fn search_tools(&self, query: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<ToolInfo>> {\n        let query = query.to_lowercase();\n        let registry = Self::load_registry().await?;\n        Ok(registry\n            .list()\n            .await\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|tool| {\n                tool.name.to_lowercase().contains(&query)\n                    || tool.description.to_lowercase().contains(&query)\n                    || tool.category.to_lowercase().contains(&query)\n     .map(|tool| ToolInfo {\n                name: tool.name,\n                description: tool.description,\n                input_schema: tool.input_schema,\n                annotations: None,\n            })\n            .collect())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Session context passed through from gateway\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct SessionContext {\n    pub session_id: Option<String>,\n SessionContext) {\n        info!(\n            session_id = ?ctx.session_id,\n            is_controller = %ctx.is_controller,\n            \"Session context set\"\n        );\n        *self.session.write().await = ctx;\n    }\n\n    /// Check if current session can execute controller-only tools\n    pub async fn can_execute_controller_tools(&self) -> bool {\n        self.session.read().await.is_controller\n    }\n\n    /// Handle MCP request\n    pub async fn handle_request(&self, request: McpRequest) -> McpResponse {\n        debug!(method = %request.method, Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.\n- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.\n- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. {"timestamp":"2026-07-03T08:46:08.591Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_CTirFGhbGKWIWx0wfLz7Ycm9","output":"Chunk ID: 0394b7\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 378\nOutput:\n     1\t#!/bin/bash\n     2\t# deploy/deploy.sh — Operation D-Bus system deployment (s6-rc)\n     3\t#\n     4\t# Usage:\n     5\t#   sudo ./deploy/deploy.sh [--skip-network] [SERVICE|all]\n     6\t#\n     7\t# Services: op-dbus, op-web-server, op-chat, op-services, op-projection,\n     8\t# op-dbus-mirror, op-grpc-bridge, op-mcp-compact\n     9\t\n    10\tset -euo pipefail\n    11\t\n    12\tPROJECT_ROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/..\" && pwd)\"\n    13\tDEPLOY_DIR=\"${PROJECT_ROOT}/deploy\"\n    14\tINSTALL_BIN=\"/usr/local/bin\"\n    15\tS6_SV=\"/etc/s6/sv\"\n    16\tS6_DB=\"/etc/s6/db\"\n    17\t\n    18\tSERVICES=(\n    19\t    \"op-identity:op-identity-sled:opdbus\"\n    20\t    \"op-web:op-dbus:op-dbus\"\n    21\t    \"op-web:op-web-server:op-web-server\"\n    22\t    \"op-chat:op-chat:chatmanager\"\n    23\t    \"op-dbus-mirror:ovs-dbus-init:op-dbus-mirror\"\n    24\t    \"op-projection:projection_server:op-projection\"\n    25\t    \"op-grpc-bridge:op-grpc-bridge:op-grpc-bridge\"\n    26\t    \"op-mcp:op-mcp-server:op-mcp-compact\"\n    27\t    \"op-cognitive-mcp:op-cognitive-mcp:op-cognitive-mcp\"\n    28\t)\n    29\t\n    30\t# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    31\t# Args\n    32\t# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    33\t\n    34\tSKIP_NETWORK=false\n    35\tTARGET=\"\"\n    36\t\n    37\tfor arg in \"$@\"; do\n    38\t    case \"$arg\" in\n    39\t        --skip-network) SKIP_NETWORK=true ;;\n    40\t        --help) echo \"Usage: sudo $0 [--skip-network] [SERVICE|all]\"; exit 0 ;;\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2725-2735-7700-93ea-77e826349203"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-03T08:46:15.920Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"I found two separate problems.\n\nThe deployment problem is real: `deploy/deploy.sh` was not deploying the binaries that own the blob/sled path. `/usr/local/bin/op-identity-sled`, `/usr/local/bin/op-mcp-server`, `/usr/local/bin/op-grpc-bridge`, `/usr/local/bin/op-cognitive-mcp`, and `/usr/local/bin/projection_server` were all older than the local `target/release` builds.\n\nI patched [deploy.sh](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/deploy.sh:18) so normal deploys now build/install:\n\n- `op-identity-sled`, restarting `opdbus`\n- `op-grpc-bridge`, restarting `op-grpc-bridge`\n- `op-mcp-server`, restarting `op-mcp-compact`\n- existing projection/cognitive services remain included\n\nVerification passed:\n\n- `cargo check -p op-identity -p op-grpc-bridge`\n- `bash -n deploy/deploy.sh`\n- `git diff --check -- deploy/deploy.sh`\n\nThe architecture problem is still present in source: the code is not yet using a single schema-containing blob. It still writes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` and separately writes `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`, with multiple readers still hardcoded to those paths. The deploy fix makes the blob-related binaries deploy correctly, but the true “blob includes schema” migration still needs code changes in `op-identity`, `op-projection`, and `op-grpc-bridge`.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-07-03T08:46:15.931Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","id":"msg_067aa5c8dd66a1d0016a4776e16ff08197b6b5f4700478139d","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"I found two separate problems.\n\nThe deployment problem is real: `deploy/deploy.sh` was not deploying the binaries that own the blob/sled path. `/usr/local/bin/op-identity-sled`, `/usr/local/bin/op-mcp-server`, `/usr/local/bin/op-grpc-bridge`, `/usr/local/bin/op-cognitive-mcp`, and `/usr/local/bin/projection_server` were all older than the local `target/release` builds.\n\nI patched [deploy.sh](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/deploy.sh:18) so normal deploys now build/install:\n\n- `op-identity-sled`, restarting `opdbus`\n- `op-grpc-bridge`, restarting `op-grpc-bridge`\n- `op-mcp-server`, restarting `op-mcp-compact`\n- existing projection/cognitive services remain included\n\nVerification passed:\n\n- `cargo check -p op-identity -p op-grpc-bridge`\n- `bash -n deploy/deploy.sh`\n- `git diff --check -- deploy/deploy.sh`\n\nThe architecture problem is still present in source: the code is not yet using a single schema-containing blob. It still writes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` and separately writes `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`, with multiple readers still hardcoded to those paths. This module implements a reader for the `IdentitySled` struct\n//! located in shared memory, following the 3tched Architecture principles.\n\nuse crate::interfaces::{RawEntity, SourceReader};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse op_identity::read_sled;\nuse simd_json::json;\nuse tracing::debug;\n\n/// Reader that extracts state from the Identity Sled in shared memory.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct IdentitySledReader {\n    /// Source identifier\n    source: String,\n}\n\nimpl IdentitySledReader {\n    /// Creates a new IdentitySledReader\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            source: \"identity-sled\".to_string(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for IdentitySledReader {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SourceReader for IdentitySledReader {\n    fn read_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        let mut entities = Vec::new();\n\n        match self.read_sled_entity() {\n            Ok(entity) => entities.push(entity),\n            Err(e) => debug!(\"Sled not available: {}\", e),\n        }\n\n        Ok(entities)\n    }\n\n    fn read_entity(&self, entity_id: &str) -> Result<RawEntity> {\n        if entity_id == \"current\" {\n            self.read_sled_entity()\n        } else {\n            Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"Unknown sled entity: {}\", entity_id))\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn source_id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.source\n    }\n\n    fn is_available(&self) -> bool {\n        std::path::Path::new(op_identity::SHM_SLED_PATH).exists()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IdentitySledReader {\n    fn read_sled_entity(&self) -> Result<RawEntity> {\n        let (ptr, _mmap) =\n            read_sled().map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to read sled: {}\", e))?;\n        // SAFETY: `read_sled()` returns a pointer to a valid `IdentitySled` mapped\n        // into shared memory (`/dev/shm`). The `_mmap` guard owns the mapping and\n        // keeps it alive for the duration of this borrow, so the pointer is valid.\n        let sled = unsafe { &*ptr };\n\n        let footprint = hex::encode(sled.hashed_footprint);\n        let pubkey = hex::encode(sled.wireguard_pubkey);\n\n        Ok(RawEntity {\n            entity_type: \"identity.sled\".to_string(),\n            entity_id: \"current\".to_string(),\n            data: json!({\n                \"mutation_index\": sled.mutation_index,\n                \"hashed_footprint\": footprint,\n                \"wireguard_pubkey\": pubkey,\n            }),\n            source: self.source.clone(),\n        })\n    }\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2728-c391-71d3-829d-7bdbe619dd79"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-03T08:54:19.635Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Implemented the blob architecture fix.\n\nThe schema catalog is now embedded into `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` after the fixed 152-byte `IdentitySled` prefix, so existing mmap readers still work while newer readers get the schema from the same blob artifact.\n\nKey changes:\n\n- Added versioned embedded schema blob format in [schema_bridge.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs:21): `OPBLOB01`, version, length, schema bytes.\n- `write_sled()` now preserves the embedded schema blob when WireGuard identity refresh rewrites the sled in [schema_bridge.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs:277).\n- `SchemaEngine::write_schemas_to_shm()` now writes the legacy JSON and embeds the same schema into the sled blob in [schema_engine.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/schema_engine.rs:149).\n- gRPC plugin schema discovery now reads the embedded blob first, falling back to `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` only for compatibility in [grpc_server.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs:139).\n- Updated `op-cognitive-mcp` and `op-web` schema readers to prefer the embedded blob.\n- Fixed deployment drift by adding `op-identity-sled`, `op-grpc-bridge`, and `op-mcp-server` to [deploy.sh](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/deploy.sh:18), so blob-owning binaries actually get installed.\n\nVerification passed:\n\n```sh\ncargo check -p op-identity -p op-projection -p op-grpc-bridge -p op-cognitive-mcp -p op-web\ngit diff --check -- <changed files>\n```\n\nI did not run the live deploy because it installs to `/usr/local/bin` and restarts s6 services. Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths after expanding the matching alias from `### Skill roots`.\n- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.\n- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.\n- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):\n  1) After deciding to use a skill, the main agent must expand the listed short `path` with the matching alias from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions. If a read is truncated or paginated, continue until EOF.\n  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the directory containing that expanded `SKILL.md` first, and only consider other paths if needed.\n  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, use its routing instructions to identify the files required for the task. The main agent must read each required instruction or reference file itself before acting on it. Do not delegate reading, summarizing, or interpreting skill instructions to a subagent. Subagents may still perform task work when the selected skill allows it.\n  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.\n  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.\n- Coordination and sequencing:\n  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.\n  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). {"timestamp":"2026-07-03T10:26:54.125Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-07-03</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2784-5d41-7312-96d2-b390152be061"}}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-07-03</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2799-b84a-7361-8dce-e88ed3a1cda3"}}}

subvol root, etc for Complete blobs\n    pub blob_meta: Option<BlobMeta>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]\npub struct BlobMeta {\n    /// e.g. \"zeroclaw-gemma4-ollama\"\n    pub kind: String,\n    /// path to btrfs subvol when materialized as deployable unit\n    pub btrfs_subvol: Option<PathBuf>,\n    /// model tag (gemma4:12b) or store ref\n    pub model_ref: Option<String>,\n    /// provider (ollama/local via zeroclaw)\n    pub provider_ref: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Simple blobify helper: given the schema + fd + state produce blob.\npub fn blobify_plugin_schema(\n    schema_json: &str,\n    schema_hash: u64,\n    dbus_path: &str,\n    fd_set: Vec<u8>,\n    methods: Vec<String>,\n    projected_data: Value,\n) -> Result<PluginObjectBlob> {\n    Ok(PluginObjectBlob {\n        schema_json: schema_json.to_string(),\n        schema_hash,\n        dbus_identity: dbus_path.to_string(),\n        grpc_fd_set: fd_set,\n        methods,\n        data: projected_data,\n        blob_meta: None,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Mark this blob as a full gemma4 deployment (the target for user request).\npub fn with_gemma_blob_meta(mut blob: PluginObjectBlob, subvol: Option<PathBuf>) -> PluginObjectBlob {\n    blob.blob_meta = Some(BlobMeta {\n        kind: \"zeroclaw-gemma4-ollama\".to_string(),\n        btrfs_subvol: subvol,\n        model_ref: Some(\"gemma4:12b\".to_string()),\n        provider_ref: Some(\"ollama\".to_string()),\n    });\n    blob\n}\n\n/// Example shm path convention (per conversation: hash in name)\npub fn shm_blob_path(blob: &PluginObjectBlob) -> PathBuf {\n    PathBuf::from(format!(\n        \"/dev/shm/opdbus/blobs/{:016x}.blob\",\n        blob.schema_hash\n    ))\n}\n\n// Integration hook suggestions:\n//  - In op-grpc-bridge or op-projection call blobify_plugin_schema for zeroclaw etc.\n//  - Push active PluginObjectBlob refs into an ActiveReflectionCatalog.\n//  - Use deploy/btrfs-layout style scripts to \"materialize\" a gemma blob (subvol + copy the serialized blob + record).\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n r#\"{\"plugin\":\"zeroclaw\"}\"#,\n            0xdeadbeef,\n            \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw\",\n            vec![],\n            vec![\"chat\".into()],\n            data,\n        ).unwrap();\n        let p = shm_blob_path(&b);\n        assert!(p.to_string_lossy().contains(\"deadbeef\"));\n    }\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2799-b84a-7361-8dce-e88ed3a1cda3"}}}

It landed as a mix of docs, untracked files, compiled helper types, and partial Zeroclaw state metadata, but not a working runtime path.\n\nConcrete gaps:\n\n- `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/plugin_object_blob.rs` exists and compiles, but parts are dead code.\n- `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_object_blob.rs` exists, but it only constructs a blob object locally.\n- The handoff doc claims `dynamic_reflection.rs` / `ActiveReflectionCatalog`, but that file is not present.\n- `grpc_server.rs` still uses static `FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET` reflection and still reads `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`.\n- `crates/op-projection/src/blob.rs` is mostly a packaging helper with comments saying where to hook it in.\n- `deploy/deploy-blob-gemma4.sh` writes manifest/sidecar JSON, including placeholder-style values like `synthesized-on-activation`; it does not create the actual hash-named shm blob or active reflection registration.\n- `ZeroclawState.object_blob` contains `\"schema_hash\": \"to-be-materialized\"` and empty descriptor bytes. `apply_state` still reports success without materializing anything.\n\nSo the honest answer is: effort went into describing and partially scaffolding the blob architecture, but the actual “no stubs/placeholders, native-local complete gemma4 blob through D-Bus/gRPC reflection” implementation was not completed.\n\nAfter Grok finishes recovery, the next clean target is one component only: make `op-grpc-bridge` own real `PluginObjectBlob` activation by adding the missing active catalog, writing hash-addressed blobs to `/dev/shm`, and replacing the static/live-schema reflection path for Zeroclaw first.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-03T16:46:10.131Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-07-03</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f28df-972e-7680-95ff-1ab274e6e32a"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-03T23:55:41.581Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8.
