{"timestamp":"2026-07-03T23:56:13.569Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_vTbAg8kA4L8qcOKvvF3yw0X4","output":"Chunk ID: 29f2d5\nWall time: 0.0001 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1965\nOutput:\n# Plugin Schema Uniformization\n\n# Mission: Plugin Schema Uniformization\n\n## Plan Overview\n\nMigrate ALL 46 plugins in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/` to a uniform GB.<PluginName> pattern. Each plugin gets a new `gb_<name>.rs` file created from scratch by reading the old plugin and transferring only the good parts. Common schema elements are extracted into reusable shared Rust struct definitions (composition via `#[serde(flatten)]`) to keep large schemas manageable.\n\nEach plugin migration follows a **7-step procedure** within a single worker session, covering all 7 quality dimensions: schema creation, drift guard, OSCAL subid compliance, schemars adapter usage, SideEffect/idempotency, x-oscal-subid annotations, and validation/registration/retirement.\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Common Schema Blobs (Pre-Work)\n\nSince op-blob has no existing section composition infrastructure, reusable schema sections are implemented as **shared Rust struct definitions** in a new `common_schema_fields.rs` module within op-plugins. Plugins embed these via `#[serde(flatten)]`. The structs provide typed fields with correct defaults; subids are injected post-generation via a helper function since they are plugin-specific.\n\n**Shared structs to create:**\n- `PluginMetadata`: `running: bool`, `healthy: bool`, `version: String`, `software: String`, `dependencies: Vec<String>`, `oscal_source: Option<String>`, `tools: serde_json::Value`\n- `NetworkInterface`: `name: String`, `address: String`, `mtu: u32`, `bridge_name: String`, `port: String`\n- `ServiceConfig`: `enabled: bool`, `socket_port: String`, `config_path: String`\n- `AIModelConfig`: `model_id: String`, `model_name: String`, `auth_method: String`, `available: bool`\n\nA helper `inject_common_subids(&mut PluginSchema, plugin_name: &str, sections: &[CommonSection])` adds the correct plugin-specific subids for flattened common fields after `plugin_schema_from_json`.\n\n### Plugin Migration Pattern (Per Plugin)\n\nEach migration follows the template in `plugin_scaffold.rs.template` and the gold-standard pattern from `xray.rs`:\n\n1. **Create** `gb_<name>.rs` with typed state structs (`#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` + `x-oscal-subid` annotations)\n2. **Drift guard**: Add `#[cfg(test)] fn <name>_schema_golden()` + `derived_schema_matches_hand_rolled` test using `schema_diffs`\n3. **Subid compliance**: All subids use valid categories (src, prj, sch, mut, obs, evt, exp) and component-types; `mut.*` fields have `actor_id`/`capability_id`; `src.*` fields have `source_system`/`source_locator`. Add `all_subids_are_valid` test.\n4. **Schemars adapter**: Uses `plugin_schema_from_json` + `apply_state_defaults`; methods via `method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<Input, Output>`\n5. **SideEffect & idempotency**: Every method has `SideEffect::Read` or `SideEffect::Mutation`; idempotency set (true for reads, false for mutations, true for deletes)\n6. **x-oscal-subid annotations**: Every state struct field, method input/output struct, and nested field has `#[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"...\"))]`\n7. **Validation & registration**: Add to `mod.rs`, run `cargo check/test/clippy`, retire old file (rename to `.bak`)\n\n### Worker Design\n\nTwo worker types:\n- **blob-creator**: Creates the common schema field definitions module and subid injection helper\n- **plugin-migrator**: Follows the 7-step procedure per plugin (the main worker for all 46 plugins)\n\n## Expected Functionality (Milestones)\n\n### Milestone 0: Common Schema Blobs (1 feature)\nCreate `common_schema_fields.rs` with shared struct definitions and `inject_common_subids` helper.\n\n### Milestone 1: Fix Failing CI Tests (6 features)\nMigrate the 6 plugins that cause test failures: fail2ban, persona, blockchain, json_render, openflow_obfuscation, software. This unblocks CI immediately.\n\n### Milestone 2: Network & System Plugins (8 features)\nMigrate hand-rolled network/system plugins: wireguard, ovsdb_bridge, openflow, users, s6_systemctl, login1, cozo, dnsresolver.\n\n### Milestone 3: Service & Package Plugins (8 features)\nMigrate: keyring, packagekit, pcidecl, service, s6, systemd, systemd_networkd, proxy_server.\n\n### Milestone 4: Remaining Hand-Rolled Plugins (8 features)\nMigrate: shared_unix_socket, datastore, mail_server, incus, incus_device, rovs_commands, privacy, zeroclaw.\n\n### Milestone 5: Tier 3 Plugins (10 features)\nMigrate schemars-derived plugins lacking drift guards: btrfs_plugin, factory, full_system, qdrant, embedding_model, large_language_model, gemma_brain, memory_plugin, privacy_router, freedesktop.\n\n### Milestone 6: Tier 2 Plugins (6 features)\nAdd drift guards to: config, endpoint, keypair, agent_config, antigravity, antigravity_chat.\n\n**Total: 47 features across 7 milestones.**\n\n## Environment Setup\n\n- **Rust toolchain**: Already installed (cargo, rustc, clippy)\n- **No external services needed**: Pure Rust codebase migration\n- **No credentials needed**: No external API dependencies\n- **Build commands**: `cargo check -p op-plugins`, `cargo test -p op-plugins --lib`, `cargo clippy -p op-plugins -- -D warnings`\n\n## Infrastructure\n\n**Services:** None required. This is a code-only migration mission.\n\n**Off-limits:**\n- Do NOT touch `op-dbus-mirror` crate (has unresolved merge conflicts from another branch)\n- Do NOT modify `op-grpc-bridge` (already updated in prior unification work)\n- Do NOT modify `op-blob` crate (already unified in prior work) except for the common schema fields module which goes in op-plugins\n- Do NOT start any long-running services\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Programmatic Validation (Milestone Gate)\n- **Test**: `cargo test -p op-plugins --lib` (129+ tests, must have 0 failures)\n- **Typecheck**: `cargo check -p op-plugins`\n- **Lint**: `cargo clippy -p op-plugins -- -D warnings`\n\n### Worker-Level Scoping\nWorkers should run these commands scoped to their work before handoff:\n- `cargo check -p op-plugins` (verify compilation)\n- `cargo test -p op-plugins --lib -- <plugin_name>` (run only the migrated plugin's tests)\n- `cargo clippy -p op-plugins -- -D warnings` (verify no lint issues)\n\n### User Testing Strategy\nThis mission has no browser/UI surface. All validation is programmatic via cargo commands. The validation contract assertions are all verifiable by running cargo test/check/clippy.\n\n### Key Test Targets\n- `all_plugin_subids_are_valid_and_unique` — the CI gate test that currently fails\n- Per-plugin `derived_schema_matches_hand_rolled` — drift guard\n- Per-plugin `all_subids_are_valid` — subid compliance\n- `cargo test -p op-plugins --lib` — full suite must pass with 0 failures\n\n## Mission Readiness\n\n**Verified dependencies:**\n- Rust toolchain: installed and functional (cargo check/test/clippy all run successfully)\n- op-blob crate: compiled, 16 tests pass\n- op-plugins crate: compiles, 129 tests pass, 2 known failures (to be fixed by this mission)\n- op-grpc-bridge: compiles, updated for new blob API\n- schemars 1.x: available as dependency (already in op-blob Cargo.toml)\n\n**Validation path confirmed:**\n- `cargo check -p op-plugins` — works (18s)\n- `cargo test -p op-plugins --lib` — works (1s, 131 tests)\n- `cargo clippy -p op-plugins -- -D warnings` — works (0 warnings)\n\n**Resources:** 22GB RAM, 8 CPU cores, 120GB disk free. Adequate for sequential cargo builds.\n\n## Non-Functional Requirements\n\n- **No regressions**: All 129 currently passing tests must continue to pass\n- **CI gate**: `all_plugin_subids_are_valid_and_unique` must pass after migration\n- **Determinism**: Schemars-derived schemas must be deterministic (same input → same output)\n- **Backward compatibility**: D-Bus object paths, gRPC service names, and method names must not change (the plugin name stays the same, only the file name changes to `gb_<name>.rs`)\n- **No new dependencies**: Use only existing crates (schemars, serde, simd_json, op-state-store, op-blob)","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2a68-d514-7052-9acc-c3d7cebb4b01"}}}

Weak hand-rolled schemas are replaced with typed Rust structs derived from **official source documentation** (e.g., networkmanager.dev for OVS, WireGuard docs, systemd D-Bus introspection XML, PackageKit API spec, Incus API, etc.).\n\n## Key Architectural Decisions\n\n### 1. Common Schema Blobs via Shared Rust Structs\n\nop-blob has no existing section composition infrastructure. Reusable schema sections are implemented as **shared Rust struct definitions** in a new `common_schema_fields.rs` module within op-plugins. Plugins embed these via `#[serde(flatten)]`. The structs provide typed fields with correct defaults; subids are injected post-generation via a helper function since they are plugin-specific.\n\n**Shared structs:**\n- `PluginMetadata`: `running`, `healthy`, `version`, `software`, `dependencies`, `oscal_source`, `tools`\n- `NetworkInterface`: `name`, `address`, `mtu`, `bridge_name`, `port`\n- `ServiceConfig`: `enabled`, `socket_port`, `config_path`\n- `AIModelConfig`: `model_id`, `model_name`, `auth_method`, `available`\n\nHelper: `inject_common_subids(&mut PluginSchema, plugin_name: &str, sections: &[CommonSection])` adds plugin-specific subids for flattened common fields after `plugin_schema_from_json`.\n\n### 2. Research-Driven Schema Design\n\n**This is a critical requirement.** For hand-rolled plugins with weak schemas (using `serde_json::Value` for everything, or missing typed fields), workers MUST research official sources to get structured data for proper typed Rust structs. This is NOT optional.\n\n**Research sources by plugin domain:**\n- **WireGuard**: Official WireGuard docs (wireguard.com), `wg` man pages, `wg-quick` config format\n- **OVS/OVSDB**: networkmanager.dev, Open vSwitch documentation, OVSDB RFC 7047, `ovs-vsctl` output schema\n- **OpenFlow**: OpenFlow switch specification 1.5, `ovs-ofctl` command reference\n- **systemd/login1**: systemd D-Bus introspection XML (freedesktop.org), `org.freedesktop.login1` interface docs\n- **systemd-networkd**: `org.freedesktop.network1` D-Bus interface\n- **PackageKit**: packagekit.org API docs, `org.freedesktop.PackageKit` interface\n- **s6**: skarnet.org s6 documentation, s6-rc service definition format\n- **Incus**: linuxcontainers.org/incus, Incus API reference\n- **CozoDB**: cozodb.org docs, Datalog query schema\n- **DNS resolver**: systemd-resolved D-Bus `org.freedesktop.resolve1`\n- **GNOME Keyring**: GNOME Keyring D-Bus interface wiki\n- **PCI**: `/sys/bus/pci` sysfs documentation, `lspci` output format\n- **Mail server**: Postfix/Dovecot config schema docs\n- **fail2ban**: fail2ban.org manual, jail.conf schema\n- **persona**: Agent persona catalog from op-agents crate\n\nWorkers use WebSearch and FetchUrl tools to access these sources. If a worker cannot find official documentation, they should ask the user rather than guessing.\n\n### 3. Plugin Migration Pattern (7-Step Procedure)\n\nEach migration follows the template in `plugin_scaffold.rs.template` and the gold-standard pattern from `xray.rs`:\n\n**Step 1 - Schema Location & Validation:**\n- Read the ENTIRE old plugin file\n- Read the template and xray.rs reference\n- Research official sources if the old schema is weak (hand-rolled, uses `serde_json::Value`, missing typed fields)\n- Create NEW file `gb_<name>.rs` with typed state structs (`#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` + `x-oscal-subid`)\n- Transfer plugin identity (name, version, category, description)\n- Reference common blobs where applicable via `#[serde(flatten)]`\n- Write PLUGIN ENTRY and PLUGIN BODY sections\n\n**Step 2 - Drift Guard:**\n- Create `#[cfg(test)] fn <name>_schema_golden()` reproducing the old hand-rolled schema\n- Add `derived_schema_matches_hand_rolled` test using `schema_diffs`\n- Fix any schema drift (update golden to match correct derived schema)\n\n**Step 3 - OSCAL Subid Compliance:**\n- All subids use valid categories (src, prj, sch, mut, obs, evt, exp)\n- All subids use valid component-types (software, service, network, hardware, process-procedure, standard, validation, policy, plan, guidance, physical, this-system, system, interconnection)\n- `mut.*` subids: ensure `actor_id` and `capability_id` fields exist\n- `src.*` subids: ensure `source_system` and `source_locator` fields exist\n- `evt.*` subids: ensure `event_id` or `event_hash` fields exist\n- Add `all_subids_are_valid` test\n\n**Step 4 - Schemars Adapter & Typed Methods:**\n- Uses `plugin_schema_from_json` (not hand-rolled `PluginSchema { ... }`)\n- `apply_state_defaults` called\n- Methods via `method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<Input, Output>`\n- If old plugin had no methods, add at minimum `get_status` (Read) and `set_status` (Mutation)\n\n**Step 5 - SideEffect & Idempotency:**\n- Every method has `SideEffect::Read` or `SideEffect::Mutation`\n- Idempotency: true for reads, false for mutations, true for deletes\n- Every method has a capability string\n\n**Step 6 - x-oscal-subid Annotations:**\n- Every state struct field has `#[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"...\"))]`\n- Every method input/output struct has x-oscal-subid on struct and each field\n- Root state struct has schema-level x-oscal-subid\n- Subid format: `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@v1]`\n\n**Step 7 - Validation, Registration & Retirement:**\n- Add `pub mod gb_<name>;` to mod.rs\n- Add `pub use gb_<name>::Gb<Name>Plugin;` to mod.rs re-exports\n- Verify `inventory::submit!` for self-registration\n- Run `cargo check -p op-plugins`\n- Run `cargo test -p op-plugins --lib -- <name>`\n- Run `cargo clippy -p op-plugins -- -D warnings`\n- Rename old file to `<name>.rs.bak`\n- Remove old `pub mod <name>;` from mod.rs if it conflicts\n- Run full `cargo test -p op-plugins --lib` to verify no regressions\n\n### 4. File Structure\n\n```\ncrates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/\n├── common_schema_fields.rs     # NEW: shared struct definitions + inject_common_subids\n├── gb_fail2ban.rs              # NEW: replaces fail2ban.rs\n├── gb_persona.rs               # NEW: replaces persona.rs\n├── gb_blockchain_plugin.rs     # NEW: replaces blockchain_plugin.rs\n├── gb_json_render.rs           # NEW: replaces json_render.rs\n├── gb_openflow_obfuscation.rs  # NEW: replaces openflow_obfuscation.rs\n├── gb_software.rs              # NEW: replaces software.rs\n├── gb_wireguard.rs             # NEW: replaces wireguard.rs\n├── ... Plugin Identity Preservation\n\nThe plugin name stays the same (e.g., \"fail2ban\"), only the file name changes to `gb_fail2ban.rs`. I did not edit anything.\n\n**Findings**\n\n- **Blocker:** `cargo check -p op-plugins` fails with **64 errors**, so the plugin work is not buildable. First failures are malformed generated Rust, e.g. [gb_antigravity.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gb_antigravity.rs:735), [gb_cognitive_mcp.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gb_cognitive_mcp.rs:749), and stray prose inside code at [gb_shared_unix_socket.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gb_shared_unix_socket.rs:451).\n\n- **Blocker:** plugin registration is inconsistent. [mod.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/mod.rs:16) still declares many legacy modules beside `gb_*` modules, while some old modules are commented out. This causes stale references like [lib.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/lib.rs:71) still calling `state_plugins::cognitive_mcp`, which no longer exists.\n\n- **Blocker:** several generated plugins do not implement the current `StatePlugin` trait. [gb_incus_device.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gb_incus_device.rs:903) uses obsolete methods/signatures, while the trait requires `apply_state(&StateDiff)`, `verify_state`, `create_checkpoint`, and `rollback(&Checkpoint)` in [plugin.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-state/src/plugin.rs:146).\n\n- **Major architecture drift:** the mission scoped common schema structs into `op-plugins`, but the work added/referenced `op-blob` as the new adapter/common-section authority: [Cargo.toml](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/Cargo.toml:15), [crates/op-plugins/Cargo.toml](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/Cargo.toml:20), [common_schema_fields.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/common_schema_fields.rs:12). That violates the mission boundary and expands the blast radius.\n\n- **Major:** generated common-field usage is mechanically inconsistent. Example: [gb_btrfs_plugin.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gb_btrfs_plugin.rs:659) calls `inject_common_subids(&mut schema)`, but the actual helper requires `schema, plugin_name, sections`.\n\n- **Major:** some generated struct changes are invalid Rust/schema usage, not just wiring. Example: [gb_s6_systemctl.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gb_s6_systemctl.rs:166) derives `PartialEq` on a struct containing `PluginMetadata`, but that type does not implement `PartialEq`; line [411](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gb_s6_systemctl.rs:411) also inserts `metadata` into the wrong struct initializer.\n\n**Bottom line:** the plugin mission is not almost complete. It has a lot of generated files, but it is currently pre-compile and has architecture drift. The fastest recovery path is to freeze the broad migration, get one small milestone compiling first, and remove either the legacy or GB module path per plugin instead of keeping both.\n\nValidation run: `cargo check -p op-plugins` failed; no tests or clippy could be meaningfully run after that.\n\n","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":{"entries":[{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":266,"lineEnd":300,"note":"factory mission config context and prior ~/.factory mission routing"},{"path":"MEMORY.md","lineStart":1,"lineEnd":55,"note":"operation-dbus-proto schema-first architecture context"}],"rolloutIds":["019f0b72-7fd4-7de2-b90e-a31be8ed412e","019f0ce5-cfd2-7910-b524-3f7910d959e8","019f0eab-780d-71e3-85e4-fee9bdfa1248"]}}}

     .version(version)\n        .description(description)\n        .build();\n    schema.fields = fields;\n    schema.subids = subids;\n    // Struct-level `#[schemars(extend(\"x-immutable-paths\" = [...]))]` → immutable_paths.\n    if let Some(paths) = root.get(\"x-immutable-paths\").and_then(JVal::as_array) {\n        schema.immutable_paths = paths\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))\n            .collect();\n    }\n    schema\n}\n\n/// Follow a single `$ref` into `$defs`/`definitions`, recursively.\nfn resolve<'a>(node: &'a JVal, defs: Option<&'a Map<String, JVal>>) -> &'a JVal {\n    if let (Some(r), Some(d)) = (node.get(\"$ref\").and_then(JVal::as_str), defs) {\n        if let Some(key) = r.rsplit('/').next() {\n            if let Some(target) = d.get(key) {\n                return resolve(target, defs);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    node\n}\n\nfn required_set(node: &JVal) -> HashSet<String> {\n    node.get(\"required\")\n        .and_then(JVal::as_array)\n        .map(|a| {\n            a.iter()\n                .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))\n                .collect()\n        })\n        .unwrap_or_default()\n}\n\nfn field_type(node: &JVal, defs: Option<&Map<String, JVal>>) -> FieldType {\n    let node = resolve(node, defs);\n\n    // `anyOf`/`oneOf` covers two distinct schemars patterns:\n    //   * `Option<T>` (and other single-real-branch unions) emit one non-null\n    //     alternative plus a `null` alternative -> collapse to the concrete type.\n    //   * A `#[serde(tag = \"...\")]` enum emits one object alternative per\n    //     variant -> build a real `FieldType::OneOf` discriminated union so all\n    //     variants render instead of silently dropping all but the first.\n    if let Some(alternatives) = node\n        .get(\"anyOf\")\n        .or_else(|| node.get(\"oneOf\"))\n        .and_then(JVal::as_array)\n    {\n        let non_null: Vec<&JVal> = alternatives\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|a| type_str(a) != Some(\"null\"))\n            .collect();\n        match non_null.as_slice() {\n            [] => {}\n            [single] => return field_type(single, defs),\n            many => {\n                return FieldType::OneOf(many.iter().map(|a| field_type(a, defs)).collect());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if let Some(en) = node.get(\"enum\").and_then(JVal::as_array) {\n        return FieldType::Enum(\n            en.iter()\n                .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))\n                .collect(),\n        );\n    }\n\n    match type_str(node) {\n        Some(\"string\") => FieldType::String,\n        Some(\"integer\") => FieldType::Integer,\n        Some(\"number\") => FieldType::Float,\n        Some(\"boolean\") => FieldType::Boolean,\n        Some(\"array\") => {\n            let item = node\n                .get(\"items\")\n                .map(|i| field_type(i, defs))\n                .unwrap_or(FieldType::Any);\n            FieldType::Array(Box::new(item))\n        }\n        Some(\"object\") => {\n            let req = required_set(node);\n            let mut m = HashMap::new();\n            if let Some(props) = node.get(\"properties\").and_then(JVal::as_object) {\n                for (k, v) in props {\n                    m.insert(k.clone(), field_schema(v, defs, req.contains(k.as_str())));\n                }\n            }\n            FieldType::Object(m)\n        }\n        _ => FieldType::Any,\n    }\n}\n\n/// schemars emits `\"type\": \"string\"` or, for `Option<T>`, `\"type\": [\"string\",\"null\"]`.\n/// Collapse to the first non-null type.\nfn type_str(node: &JVal) -> Option<&str> {\n    match node.get(\"type\") {\n        Some(JVal::String(s)) => Some(s.as_str()),\n        Some(JVal::Array(a)) => a.iter().filter_map(JVal::as_str).find(|t| *t != \"null\"),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn field_schema(node: &JVal, defs: Option<&Map<String, JVal>>, required: bool) -> FieldSchema {\n    // Metadata such as `description`, `examples`, `readOnly`, and `default` are\n    // declared on the field node itself; only the type/reference needs to be\n    // resolved through `$defs`.\n    let meta = node;\n    FieldSchema {\n        field_type: field_type(node, defs),\n        required,\n        description: meta\n            .get(\"description\")\n            .and_then(JVal::as_str)\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n            .to_string(),\n        default: meta.get(\"default\").map(to_simd),\n        example: example_of(meta).map(to_simd),\n        constraints: constraints(meta),\n        read_only: meta\n            .get(\"readOnly\")\n            .and_then(JVal::as_bool)\n            .unwrap_or(false),\n        read_only_when: None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn example_of(node: &JVal) -> Option<&JVal> {\n    if let Some(first) = node\n        .get(\"examples\")\n        .and_then(JVal::as_array)\n        .and_then(|a| a.first())\n    {\n        return Some(first);\n    }\n    node.get(\"example\")\n}\n\nfn constraints(node: &JVal) -> Vec<Constraint> .unwrap_or_else(|| b\"{}\".to_vec()),\n        })\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    methods.sort_by(|left, right| left.schema_name.cmp(&right.schema_name));\n\n    PluginObjectBlob {\n        plugin_id: plugin_id.to_string(),\n        schema_version: schema.version.clone(),\n        schema_hash,\n        schema_json,\n        dbus,\n        grpc: GrpcObjectIdentity {\n            package: grpc_package,\n                grpc_service_name,\n                &schema,\n            ),\n        },\n        methods,\n    }\n}\n\npub fn synthesize_plugin_descriptor_set(\n    plugin_id: &str,\n The blob couples the four identities that must not drift:\n//! schema identity (canonical JSON + sha256), D-Bus identity, gRPC identity,\n//! and the reflection descriptor identity. It is deliberately redundant at the\n//! blob boundary: schema stays authoritative, but the blob is self-describing\n//! enough that reflection, GUI, compliance, and dispatch reason about the same\n//! object without reassembling identity from scattered files.\n//!\n//! ## Sealed byte format (zero-copy)\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! offset  size  content\n//! 0       8     magic \"OPBLOB01\"\n//! 8       2     format version (u16 LE) = 1\n//! 10      2     section count (u16 LE)\n//! 12      4     reserved\n//! 16      32    sha256 of the SCHEMA_JSON section (the schema hash)\n//! 48      16    reserved\n//! 64      24*n  section table: tag u32, reserved u32, offset u64, len u64\n//! ...           8-byte-aligned section payloads\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Sections: 1 = canonical `PluginSchema` JSON, 2 = `BlobManifest` JSON,\n//! 3 = protobuf `FileDescriptorSet`, 4 = compliance/extra metadata JSON.\n//!\n//! `BlobRef` verifies magic + hash once, then hands out borrowed slices —\n//! reads never copy or re-parse the payload. Sealed bytes are fully\n//! deterministic for the same schema (sorted maps, no timestamps), so the\n//! schema hash doubles as the artifact identity in the filename:\n//! `<plugin_id>.<hash16>.blob`.\n\nuse crate::descriptor;\nuse crate::schema::{hex, PluginSchema, SideEffect};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse sha2::{Digest, Sha256};\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\npub const MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b\"OPBLOB01\";\npub const FORMAT_VERSION: u16 = 1;\n\npub const SECTION_SCHEMA_JSON: u32 = 1;\npub const SECTION_MANIFEST_JSON: u32 = 2;\npub const SECTION_DESCRIPTOR_SET: u32 = 3;\npub const SECTION_META_JSON: u32 = 4;\n\nconst HEADER_LEN: usize = 64;\nconst SECTION_ENTRY_LEN: usize = 24;\n\n/// D-Bus identity carried by the blob (REQ-7.1/7.2).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct DbusIdentity {\n    pub bus_name: String,\n    pub object_path: String,\n    pub interface_name: String,\n}\n\n/// gRPC identity: per-method packages/services synthesized from the schema.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct GrpcIdentity {\n    /// Fully-qualified service names, sorted.\n    pub services: Vec<String>,\n    /// Descriptor file names, sorted (parallel to services).\n    pub files: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// Per-method manifest entry copied from `PluginSchema.methods` plus the\n/// synthesized gRPC identity — the compliance/audit unit.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct MethodManifest {\n    pub schema_name: String,\n    pub grpc_name: String,\n    pub grpc_path: String,\n    pub grpc_service: String,\n    pub grpc_file: String,\n    pub input_message: String,\n    pub output_message: String,\n    pub subid: String,\n    pub required_capability: Option<String>,\n    pub side_effect: SideEffect,\n    pub idempotent: bool,\n    /// Fully-qualified symbols the method's descriptor file defines.\n    pub symbols: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// The blob's self-describing metadata (section 2).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct BlobManifest {\n    pub plugin_id: String,\n    pub schema_version: String,\n    pub schema_hash: String,\n    pub dbus: DbusIdentity,\n    pub grpc: GrpcIdentity,\n    /// WireGuard-keypair identity of the publishing account (public half\n    /// only); its session persists for the life of the account.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub identity: Option<crate::identity::BlobIdentity>,\n    pub methods: Vec<MethodManifest>,\n}\n\n/// Owned, unsealed blob. `seal()` produces the immutable byte image.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PluginObjectBlob {\n    pub manifest: BlobManifest,\n    /// Canonical `PluginSchema` JSON (the authoritative contract bytes).\n    pub schema_json: String,\n    /// Encoded `google.protobuf.FileDescriptorSet` for all plugin methods.\n    pub descriptor_set: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Compliance / extra metadata (subids, immutable paths, dialect …).\n    pub meta_json: String,\n}\n\n/// Canonical D-Bus path form: lowercase, hyphens -> underscores.\npub fn canonical_plugin_id(name: &str) -> String {\n    name.to_lowercase().replace('-', \"_\")\n}\n\n/// Freeze one `PluginSchema` into a `PluginObjectBlob` (whitepaper \"Blob\n/// Creation Pipeline\" steps 3–9). The schema is the input and stays the\n/// authority; nothing here invents contract data.\npub fn blobify(schema: &PluginSchema) -> PluginObjectBlob {\n    blobify_with_identity(schema, None)\n}\n\n/// `blobify`, stamping the publishing account's WireGuard-keypair identity\n/// (public half only) into the manifest.\npub fn blobify_with_identity(\n    schema: &PluginSchema,\n    identity: Option<crate::identity::BlobIdentity>,\n) -> PluginObjectBlob {\n    let plugin_id = canonical_plugin_id(&schema.name);\n    let schema_json = schema.canonical_json();\n    let schema_hash = lines = vec![\n        format!(\"schema_name: {}\", schema.name),\n        format!(\"schema_category: {}\", schema.category),\n        format!(\"schema_version: {}\", schema.version),\n        format!(\"schema_description: {}\", schema.description.trim()),\n    ];\n\n    let mut tags = schema.tags.clone();\n    tags.sort();\n    if !tags.is_empty() {\n        lines.push(format!(\"schema_tags: {}\", tags.join(\", \")));\n    }\n\n    let mut immutable_paths = schema.immutable_paths.clone();\n    immutable_paths.sort();\n    if !immutable_paths.is_empty() {\n        lines.push(format!(\"immutable_paths: {}\", immutable_paths.join(\", \")));\n    }\n\n    let mut dependencies = schema.dependencies.clone();\n    dependencies.sort();\n    if !dependencies.is_empty() {\n        lines.push(format!(\"dependencies: {}\", dependencies.join(\", \")));\n    }\n\n    let mut field_names = schema.fields.keys().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    field_names.sort();\n\n    for field_name in field_names {\n        let Some(field_schema) = schema.fields.get(&field_name) else {\n            continue;\n        };\n\n        lines.push(format!(\n            \"field {}: type={}, required={}, read_only={}, description={}\",\n            field_name,\n            render_field_type(&field_schema.field_type),\n            field_schema.required,\n            field_schema.read_only,\n            field_schema.description.trim()\n        ));\n\n        if let Some(condition) = &field_schema.read_only_when {\n            lines.push(format!(\n                \"field {} read_only_when: {}={}\",\n                field_name, condition.property, condition.value\n            ));\n        }\n\n        if !field_schema.constraints.is_empty() {\n            let constraints = field_schema\n                .constraints\n                .iter()\n                .map(render_constraint)\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(\", \");\n            lines.push(format!(\"field {} constraints: {}\", field_name, constraints));\n        }\n    }\n\n    lines.join(\"\\n\")\n}\n\nfn render_field_type(field_type: &FieldType) -> String {\n    match field_type {\n        FieldType::String => \"string\".to_string(),\n        FieldType::Integer => \"integer\".to_string(),\n        FieldType::Float => \"float\".to_string(),\n        FieldType::Boolean => \"boolean\".to_string(),\n        FieldType::Array(inner) => format!(\"array<{}>\", render_field_type(inner)),\n        FieldType::Object(fields) => {\n            let mut names = fields.keys().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>();\n            names.sort();\n            format!(\"object<{}>\", names.join(\"|\"))\n        }\n        FieldType::Enum(values) => format!(\"enum<{}>\", values.join(\"|\")),\n        FieldType::OneOf(branches) => format!(\n            \"one_of<{}>\",\n            branches\n                .iter()\n                .map(render_field_type)\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(\"|\")\n        ),\n        FieldType::Any => \"any\".to_string(),\n    }\n}\n\nfn render_constraint(constraint: &op_state_store::Constraint) -> String {\n    match constraint {\n        op_state_store::Constraint::Min { value } => format!(\"min={value}\"),\n        op_state_store::Constraint::Max { value } => format!(\"max={value}\"),\n        op_state_store::Constraint::Pattern { regex } => format!(\"pattern={regex}\"),\n        op_state_store::Constraint::OneOf { values } => {\n            format!(\n                \"one_of={}\",\n                serde_json::to_string(values).unwrap_or_default()\n            )\n        }\n        op_state_store::Constraint::RequiresField { field } => format!(\"requires_field={field}\"),\n        op_state_store::Constraint::Custom { validator } => format!(\"custom={validator}\"),\n    }\n}\n\nfn extract_schema_title(schema_query_text: &str) -> &str {\n    schema_query_text\n        .lines()\n        .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix(\"schema_name: \"))\n        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n}\n\nfn extract_embedding(response_json: &Value) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {\n    let Some(embedding_values) = response_json\n        .get(\"data\")\n        .and_then(Value::as_array)\n        .and_then(|entries| entries.first())\n        .and_then(|entry| entry.get(\"embedding\"))\n        .and_then(Value::as_array)\n        .or_else(|| {\n            response_json\n                .get(\"embeddings\")\n                .and_then(Value::as_array)\n                .and_then(|entries| entries.first())\n                .and_then(Value::as_array)\n        })\n    else {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"Voyage embeddings response did not contain a usable embedding\"\n        ));\n    };\n\n    let mut embedding = Vec::with_capacity(embedding_values.len());\n    for value in embedding_values {\n        let number = value\n            .as_f64()\n            .context(\"Voyage embedding contained a non-numeric value\")?;\n        embedding.push(number as f32);\n    }\n\n    ensure!(!embedding.is_empty(), \"Voyage embedding response was empty\");\n Self::Project => \"project\",\n            Self::Session => \"session\",\n            Self::Database => \"database\",\n            Self::Workflow => \"workflow\",\n            Self::Agent => \"agent\",\n            Self::Cron => \"cron\",\n            Self::Custom => \"custom\",\n        };\n        write!(f, \"{}\", s)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::str::FromStr for NamespaceKind {\n    type Err = ();\n    fn from_str(s: &str) -> std::result::Result<Self, Self::Err> {\n        Ok(match s {\n            \"project\" => Self::Project,\n            \"session\" => Self::Session,\n            \"database\" => Self::Database,\n            \"workflow\" => Self::Workflow,\n            \"agent\" => Self::Agent,\n            \"cron\" => Self::Cron,\n            _ => Self::Custom,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// A named memory context.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct MemoryNamespace {\n    pub id: String,\n    /// Canonical name: \"project:op-dbus\", \"cron:backup\", \"db:ovsdb\", etc.\n    pub name: String,\n    pub kind: NamespaceKind,\n    pub description: Option<String>,\n    pub linked_task_id: Option<String>,\n    pub linked_cron: Option<String>,\n    pub Deserialize)]\npub struct MemoryEntry {\n    pub id: String,\n    pub namespace_id: String,\n    pub key: String,\n    pub value: serde_json::Value,\n    pub tags: Vec<String>,\n    pub created_at: struct CognitiveMemoryStore {\n    shuttle: Arc<CozoGraphShuttle>,\n}\n\nimpl CognitiveMemoryStore {\n    pub async fn new(shuttle: Arc<CozoGraphShuttle>) -> Result<Self> {\n        Ok(Self { shuttle })\n    }\n\n    fn run(&self, script: &str, params: Params) -> Result<NamedRows> {\n        self.shuttle\n            .db()\n            .run_script(script, params, ScriptMutability::Mutable)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"{e}\"))\n    }\n\n    pub async fn upsert_namespace(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        kind: NamespaceKind,\n        description: Option<&str>,\n        linked_task_id: Option<&str>,\n        linked_cron: Option<&str>,\n        metadata: serde_json::Value,\n    ) -> Result<MemoryNamespace> {\n        let now = Utc::now().to_rfc3339();\n        let id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();\n        let kind_str = kind.to_string();\n        let meta_str = serde_json::to_string(&metadata)?;\n\n        let q = r#\"\n            ?[name, id, kind, description, linked_task_id, linked_cron, metadata, created_at, updated_at]\n                <- [[$name, $id, $kind, $desc, $task, $cron, $meta, $now, $now]]\n            :put memory_namespaces {\n                name => id, kind, description, linked_task_id, linked_cron, metadata, created_at, updated_at\n            }\n        \"#;\n        let mut p: Params = BTreeMap::new();\n        p.insert(\"name\".into(), DataValue::Str(name.into()));\n        p.insert(\"id\".into(), DataValue::Str(id.into()));\n        p.insert(\"kind\".into(), DataValue::Str(kind_str.into()));\n        p.insert(\n            \"desc\".into(),\n            DataValue::Str(description.unwrap_or(\"\").into()),\n        );\n        p.insert(\n            \"task\".into(),\n  p.insert(\"meta\".into(), DataValue::Str(meta_str.into()));\n        p.insert(\"now\".into(), DataValue::Str(now.into()));\n        self.run(q, p).context(\"upsert namespace\")?;\n\n        self.get_namespace_by_name(name)\n            .await?\n            .context(\"namespace not found after upsert\")\n    }\n\n    pub async fn get_namespace_by_name(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<MemoryNamespace>> {\n        let q = r#\"\n            ?[name, id, kind, description, linked_task_id, linked_cron, metadata, created_at, updated_at]\n                := *memory_namespaces[name, id, kind, description, linked_task_id, linked_cron, metadata, created_at, updated_at],\n                   name = $name\n        \"#;\n        let mut p: Params = BTreeMap::new();\n        p.insert(\"name\".into(), DataValue::Str(name.into()));\n        let rows = self.run(q, p).context(\"get namespace by name\")?;\n        Ok(rows.rows.first().map(|r|             ?[name, id, kind, description, linked_task_id, linked_cron, metadata, created_at, updated_at]\n                    := *memory_namespaces[name, id, kind, description, linked_task_id, linked_cron, metadata, created_at, updated_at],\n                       kind = $k\n                :order name\n                \"#,\n                p,\n            )\n        } else {\n            (\n                r#\"\n                ?[name, id, kind, description, linked_task_id, linked_cron, metadata, created_at, updated_at]\n                    := *memory_namespaces[name, id, kind, description, linked_task_id, linked_cron, metadata, created_at, updated_at]\n                :order name\n                \"#,\n                BTreeMap::new(),\n            )\n        };\n        let rows = self.run(q, params).context(\"list namespaces\")?;\n        Ok(rows.rows.iter().map(|r| row_to_namespace(r)).collect())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn delete_namespace(&self, name: &str) -> Result<bool> {\n        // Pre-check whether it exists; cozo :rm is silent.\n        if self.get_namespace_by_name(name).await?.is_none() {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        // Cascade: remove all entries in this namespace first.\n        let entries_q = r#\"\n            ?[ns, key]\n                := *memory_entries[ns, key, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _],\n                   ns = $ns\n        \"#;\n        let mut p: Params = BTreeMap::new();\n        p.insert(\"ns\".into(), DataValue::Str(name.into()));\n        let entry_rows = self\n            .run(entries_q, p)\n dv_as_str(&row[1]).unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n            let mut pe: Params = BTreeMap::new();\n            pe.insert(\"ns\".into(), DataValue::Str(ns.into()));\n            pe.insert(\"key\".into(), DataValue::Str(key.into()));\n            self.run(\n                \"?[namespace, key] <- [[$ns, $key]] :rm memory_entries { namespace, key }\",\n                pe,\n            )\n            .context(\"cascade delete entry\")?;\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2a6f-fdc7-71a3-8efe-a8fe7729603c"}}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. {"timestamp":"2026-07-04T00:28:56.693Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Quick quality check, no edits made.\n\n**Findings**\n1. **Netmaker is the weakest schema.** [netmaker.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/netmaker.rs:15) is too hand-shaped and not source-shaped enough. It has minimal `enabled/default_network/enrollment_token/api_endpoint`, but the runtime source model should likely reflect real `netclient` config/state more deeply. Peer discovery is explicitly stubbed/TODO at [netmaker.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/netmaker.rs:251), and read methods like `list_nodes`, `get_node`, `list_networks` currently declare `AckOutput` instead of structured source-shaped outputs at [netmaker.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/netmaker.rs:615). Also missing field-level OSCAL subids.\n\n2. **Antigravity is broad but not tight enough.** It has good coverage and subids, but some SDK concepts are weakly typed. Generation controls are plain numeric fields without schema constraints/ranges at [antigravity.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/antigravity.rs:281). google.protobuf.Timestamp verified_at = 9;\n}\n\nmessage RegisterUserRequest {\n  string email = 1;\n  string wireguard_public_key = 2;\n  string domain = 3;\n  bool is_admin = 4;\n  optional google.protobuf.Struct metadata = 5;\n}\n\nmessage RegisterUserResponse {\n  bool success = 1;\n  string user_id = 2;\n  string message = 3;\n  string assigned_ip = 4;\n  string wireguard_config = 5;\n  google.protobuf.Timestamp registered_at = 6;\n}\n\nmessage GetUserStatusRequest {\n  string email = 1;\n  string user_id = 2;\n  string domain = 3;\n}\n\nmessage GetUserStatusResponse {\n  bool registered = 1;\n  string user_id = 2;\n  string email = 3;\n  bool email_verified = 4;\n  string wireguard_public_key = 5;\n  string assigned_ip = 6;\n  bool is_admin = 7;\n  google.protobuf.Timestamp registered_at = 8;\n  google.protobuf.Timestamp last_active = 9;\n}\n\nmessage ListUsersRequest {\n  uint32 limit = 1;\n  uint32 offset = 2;\n  bool include_admins_only = google.protobuf.Timestamp last_active = 8;\n  optional google.protobuf.Struct metadata = 9;\n}\n\nmessage GetWireGuardConfigRequest {\n  string email = 1;\n  string user_id = 2;\n  string domain = google.protobuf.Timestamp generated_at = 6;\n}\n\nmessage AdminUserActionRequest {\n  string action = 1; // \"suspend\", \"unsuspend\", \"delete\", \"reset_password\"\n  string user_id = 2;\n  string {"timestamp":"2026-07-04T00:29:34.001Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_vM8ox7kEYnVqK2MCheojhk0j","output":"Chunk ID: 74543c\nWall time: 0.0001 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1995\nOutput:\n#!/bin/sh\n# Provision a workspace subscriber — full container + memory setup.\n#\n# Creates an Incus container, configures networking, provisions memory\n# namespaces and feature flags. This is the template run at signup.\n#\n# Identity chain: MAC address (user-provided shared key) -> WG keypair ->\n#   full pubkey stored in CozoDB -> MCP token = UUID v5(pubkey).\n# The MAC is less identifying than IP but hardware-bound to the user.\n#\n# Email is stored ONLY when GhostBridge is disabled. GhostBridge users\n# route through the privacy layer and must not have email in CozoDB.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh <username> --mac <aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff> --psk <key> [--email <addr>] [--ghostbridge] [--semantic]\n#\nset -eu\n\nUSERNAME=\"${1:?username required}\"\nshift\n\nMAC_ADDR=\"\"\nPSK=\"\"\nEMAIL=\"\"\nGHOSTBRIDGE=false\nSEMANTIC=false\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --mac)         shift; MAC_ADDR=\"${1:?--mac requires a MAC address}\" ;;\n        --psk)         shift; PSK=\"${1:?--psk requires a pre-shared key}\" ;;\n        --email)       shift; EMAIL=\"${1:?--email requires an address}\" ;;\n        --ghostbridge) GHOSTBRIDGE=true ;;\n        --semantic)    SEMANTIC=true ;;\n        *) echo \"Unknown option: $1\" >&2; exit 1 ;;\n    esac\n    shift\ndone\n\nCONTAINER_ID=\"ws-${USERNAME}\"\nIMAGE=\"images:debian/12\"\nMCP=\"http://100.90.37.254:3003/mcp\"\n\necho \"=== Provisioning workspace subscriber: $USERNAME ===\"\necho \"    Container  : $CONTAINER_ID\"\necho \"    MAC address: ${MAC_ADDR:-<not provided>}\"\necho \"    PSK        : ${PSK:+<provided>}${PSK:-<not provided>}\"\necho \"    Email      : ${EMAIL:-<not provided>}\"\necho \"    GhostBridge: $GHOSTBRIDGE\"\necho \"    Semantic   : $SEMANTIC\"\necho \"\"\n\n# ── 1. Create Incus container ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\necho \"[1] Creating container...\"\nif incus info \"$CONTAINER_ID\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"    Already exists — skipping\"\nelse\n    incus launch \"$IMAGE\" \"$CONTAINER_ID\"\n    echo \"    Launched $CONTAINER_ID\"\nfi\n\n# Wait for container to be ready\necho \"    Waiting for init...\"\nsleep 3\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- sh -c \"until [ -f /run/systemd/private ] || [ -d /run/s6 ] || pgrep -x init >/dev/null 2>&1 || sleep 1; do sleep 1; done\" 2>/dev/null || sleep 2\n\n# ── 2. Base packages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\necho \"[2] Installing base packages...\"\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- apt-get update -qq\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \\\n    curl ca-certificates wireguard-tools iproute2 \\\n    nodejs npm 2>/dev/null || true\n\n# ── 3. WireGuard identity — always provisioned ─────────────────────────────────\n# The WG pubkey IS the identity. The MCP token is a UUID v5 derivative.\n# The full pubkey is stored in the user database (CozoDB).\necho \"[3] Generating WireGuard identity...\"\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- sh -c \"\n    mkdir -p /etc/wireguard\n    wg genkey | tee /etc/wireguard/privkey | wg pubkey > /etc/wireguard/pubkey\n    chmod 600 /etc/wireguard/privkey\n\"\nPEER_PUBKEY=$(incus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- cat /etc/wireguard/pubkey)\necho \"    Peer pubkey: $PEER_PUBKEY\"\n\n# Derive MCP bearer token: UUID v5 from WG pubkey (one-way, not the raw key)\nTOKEN=$(uuidgen -v5 -n @oid -N \"$PEER_PUBKEY\")\necho \"    MCP token : $TOKEN (derived from pubkey)\"\n\n# GhostBridge networking (optional WG peer registration)\nif [ \"$GHOSTBRIDGE\" = \"true\" ]; then\n    echo \"    GhostBridge: registering WireGuard peer...\"\n    # TODO: register peer with Netmaker API\n    echo \"    (Netmaker registration: TODO — wire to Netmaker API)\"\nelse\n    echo \"    GhostBridge: skipped (networking only — identity already provisioned)\"\nfi\n\n# ── 4. Semantic search — Qdrant collection ────────────────────────────────────\nif [ \"$SEMANTIC\" = \"true\" ]; then\n    echo \"[4] Semantic search: enabled — Qdrant collection will be created on first use\"\nelse\n    echo \"[4] Semantic search: skipped (disabled)\"\nfi\n\n# ── 5. Memory namespaces via cognitive-mcp ────────────────────────────────────\necho \"[5] Provisioning memory namespaces...\"\n\nremember() {\n    NS=\"$1\"; KEY=\"$2\"; VAL=\"$3\"\n    RESULT=$(curl -sf -X POST \"$MCP\" \\\n        -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n        -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\\n        -H \"User-Agent: op-dbus/1.0\" \\\n        -d \"{\\\"jsonrpc\\\":\\\"2.0\\\",\\\"id\\\":1,\\\"method\\\":\\\"tools/call\\\",\\\"params\\\":{\\\"name\\\":\\\"cognitive_memory\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":{\\\"operation\\\":\\\"store\\\",\\\"namespace\\\":\\\"$NS\\\",\\\"key\\\":\\\"$KEY\\\",\\\"value\\\":$VAL}}}\" 2>&1) \\\n        && echo \"    ok: $NS/$KEY\" \\\n        || echo \"    WARN: could not write $NS/$KEY (cognitive-mcp may be unreachable)\"\n}\n\nNOW=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\n\n# Identity — cryptographic + hardware keys in CozoDB\nremember \"container:${CONTAINER_ID}:identity\" \"wireguard_pubkey\" \\\n    \"\\\"$PEER_PUBKEY\\\"\"\nremember \"container:${CONTAINER_ID}:identity\" \"mcp_token\" \\\n    \"\\\"$TOKEN\\\"\"\nif [ -n \"$MAC_ADDR\" ]; then\n    remember \"container:${CONTAINER_ID}:identity\" \"mac_address\" \\\n        \"\\\"$MAC_ADDR\\\"\"\nfi\nif [ -n \"$PSK\" ]; then\n    remember \"container:${CONTAINER_ID}:identity\" \"psk\" \\\n        \"\\\"$PSK\\\"\"\nfi\n\n# Email: store ONLY when GhostBridge is disabled.\n# GhostBridge users route through the privacy layer — email must not leak into CozoDB.\nif [ -n \"$EMAIL\" ] && [ \"$GHOSTBRIDGE\" = \"false\" ]; The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. {error}\"),\n    })\n}\n\nfn require_str(\n    args: &JsonValue,\n    field: &str,\n    method: &str,\n) -> std::result::Result<String, ZeroclawError> {\n    args.get(field)\n        .and_then(JsonValue::as_str)\n        .map(str::to_string)\n        .ok_or_else(|| ZeroclawError::ExecutionDenied {\n            reason: format!(\"{method} requires string field '{field}'\"),\n        })\n}\n\nfn resolve_route(\n    json_args: &str,\n    state: &ZeroclawState,\n) -> std::result::Result<JsonValue, ZeroclawError> {\n    let args = parse_args(\"ResolveRoute\", json_args)?;\n    let hint = require_str(&args, \"hint\", \"ResolveRoute\")?;\n    state\n        .projection\n        .model_routes\n        .iter()\n        .find(|route| route.hint == hint || route.model == hint)\n        .map(|route| serde_json::json!({ \"route\": to_json(route) }))\n        .ok_or(ZeroclawError::RouteNotDeclared { hint })\n}\n\nfn set_provider_handler(\n    json_args: &str,\n    state: &ZeroclawState,\n) -> std::result::Result<DispatchOutcome, ZeroclawError> {\n    let args = parse_args(\"SetProvider\", json_args)?;\n    let provider_id = require_str(&args, \"provider_id\", \"SetProvider\")?;\n    if !state\n        .projection\n        .providers\n        .iter()\n        .any(|p| p.id == provider_id)\n    {\n        return Err(ZeroclawError::ProviderNotDeclared {\n            provider: provider_id,\n        });\n    }\n    let old = state.selected_provider.clone();\n    Ok(DispatchOutcome {\n        result: serde_json::json!({ \"selected_provider\": provider_id }),\n        signal: Some(DispatchSignal {\n            name: \"ProviderChanged\".to_string(),\n            payload: serde_json::json!({ \"old\": old, \"new\": provider_id, \"reason\": \"explicit set\" }),\n        }),\n    })\n}\n\nfn set_model_handler(\n    json_args: &str,\n    state: &ZeroclawState,\n) -> std::result::Result<DispatchOutcome, ZeroclawError> {\n    let args = parse_args(\"SetModel\", json_args)?;\n    let model_id = require_str(&args, \"model_id\", \"SetModel\")?;\n    if !state\n        .projection\n        .model_routes\n        .iter()\n        .any(|r| r.model == model_id)\n    {\n        return Err(ZeroclawError::ModelNotDeclared { model: model_id });\n    }\n    let old = state.selected_model.clone();\n    Ok(DispatchOutcome {\n        result: serde_json::json!({ \"selected_model\": model_id }),\n        signal: Some(DispatchSignal {\n            name: \"ModelChanged\".to_string(),\n            payload: serde_json::json!({ \"old\": old, \"new\": model_id, \"reason\": \"explicit set\" }),\n        }),\n    })\n}\n\nfn set_role_model_handler(\n    json_args: &str,\n    state: &ZeroclawState,\n    role: &str,\n) -> serde_json::json!({ \"vectorization\": model_id }),\n        \"qdrant_retrieval\" => serde_json::json!({ \"qdrant_retrieval\": model_id }),\n        \"cozo_retrieval\" => serde_json::json!({ \"cozo_retrieval\": model_id }),\n        _ => {\n            return Err(ZeroclawError::ExecutionDenied {\n                reason: format!(\"unknown model role: {role}\"),\n            })\n        }\n    };\n    let signal = serde_json::json!({\n        \"role\": role,\n        \"model_id\": model_id,\n        \"selected_provider\": state.selected_provider,\n    });\n    Ok(DispatchOutcome {\n        result,\n        signal: Some(DispatchSignal {\n            name: \"ModelRoleChanged\".to_string(),\n            payload: signal,\n        }),\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use {"timestamp":"2026-07-04T00:33:37.715Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_8DrgZ9tiOl82pQlHEM47mcib","output":"Chunk ID: 96dd8a\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1995\nOutput:\n#!/bin/sh\n# Provision a workspace subscriber — full container + memory setup.\n#\n# Creates an Incus container, configures networking, provisions memory\n# namespaces and feature flags. This is the template run at signup.\n#\n# Identity chain: MAC address (user-provided shared key) -> WG keypair ->\n#   full pubkey stored in CozoDB -> MCP token = UUID v5(pubkey).\n# The MAC is less identifying than IP but hardware-bound to the user.\n#\n# Email is stored ONLY when GhostBridge is disabled. GhostBridge users\n# route through the privacy layer and must not have email in CozoDB.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh <username> --mac <aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff> --psk <key> [--email <addr>] [--ghostbridge] [--semantic]\n#\nset -eu\n\nUSERNAME=\"${1:?username required}\"\nshift\n\nMAC_ADDR=\"\"\nPSK=\"\"\nEMAIL=\"\"\nGHOSTBRIDGE=false\nSEMANTIC=false\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --mac)         shift; MAC_ADDR=\"${1:?--mac requires a MAC address}\" ;;\n        --psk)         shift; PSK=\"${1:?--psk requires a pre-shared key}\" ;;\n        --email)       shift; EMAIL=\"${1:?--email requires an address}\" ;;\n        --ghostbridge) GHOSTBRIDGE=true ;;\n        --semantic)    SEMANTIC=true ;;\n        *) echo \"Unknown option: $1\" >&2; exit 1 ;;\n    esac\n    shift\ndone\n\nCONTAINER_ID=\"ws-${USERNAME}\"\nIMAGE=\"images:debian/12\"\nMCP=\"http://100.90.37.254:3003/mcp\"\n\necho \"=== Provisioning workspace subscriber: $USERNAME ===\"\necho \"    Container  : $CONTAINER_ID\"\necho \"    MAC address: ${MAC_ADDR:-<not provided>}\"\necho \"    PSK        : ${PSK:+<provided>}${PSK:-<not provided>}\"\necho \"    Email      : ${EMAIL:-<not provided>}\"\necho \"    GhostBridge: $GHOSTBRIDGE\"\necho \"    Semantic   : $SEMANTIC\"\necho \"\"\n\n# ── 1. Create Incus container ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\necho \"[1] Creating container...\"\nif incus info \"$CONTAINER_ID\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"    Already exists — skipping\"\nelse\n    incus launch \"$IMAGE\" \"$CONTAINER_ID\"\n    echo \"    Launched $CONTAINER_ID\"\nfi\n\n# Wait for container to be ready\necho \"    Waiting for init...\"\nsleep 3\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- sh -c \"until [ -f /run/systemd/private ] || [ -d /run/s6 ] || pgrep -x init >/dev/null 2>&1 || sleep 1; do sleep 1; done\" 2>/dev/null || sleep 2\n\n# ── 2. Base packages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\necho \"[2] Installing base packages...\"\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- apt-get update -qq\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \\\n    curl ca-certificates wireguard-tools iproute2 \\\n    nodejs npm 2>/dev/null || true\n\n# ── 3. WireGuard identity — always provisioned ─────────────────────────────────\n# The WG pubkey IS the identity. The MCP token is a UUID v5 derivative.\n# The full pubkey is stored in the user database (CozoDB).\necho \"[3] Generating WireGuard identity...\"\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- sh -c \"\n    mkdir -p /etc/wireguard\n    wg genkey | tee /etc/wireguard/privkey | wg pubkey > /etc/wireguard/pubkey\n    chmod 600 /etc/wireguard/privkey\n\"\nPEER_PUBKEY=$(incus exec \"$CONTAINER_ID\" -- cat /etc/wireguard/pubkey)\necho \"    Peer pubkey: $PEER_PUBKEY\"\n\n# Derive MCP bearer token: UUID v5 from WG pubkey (one-way, not the raw key)\nTOKEN=$(uuidgen -v5 -n @oid -N \"$PEER_PUBKEY\")\necho \"    MCP token : $TOKEN (derived from pubkey)\"\n\n# GhostBridge networking (optional WG peer registration)\nif [ \"$GHOSTBRIDGE\" = \"true\" ]; then\n    echo \"    GhostBridge: registering WireGuard peer...\"\n    # TODO: register peer with Netmaker API\n    echo \"    (Netmaker registration: TODO — wire to Netmaker API)\"\nelse\n    echo \"    GhostBridge: skipped (networking only — identity already provisioned)\"\nfi\n\n# ── 4. Semantic search — Qdrant collection ────────────────────────────────────\nif [ \"$SEMANTIC\" = \"true\" ]; then\n    echo \"[4] Semantic search: enabled — Qdrant collection will be created on first use\"\nelse\n    echo \"[4] Semantic search: skipped (disabled)\"\nfi\n\n# ── 5. Memory namespaces via cognitive-mcp ────────────────────────────────────\necho \"[5] Provisioning memory namespaces...\"\n\nremember() {\n    NS=\"$1\"; KEY=\"$2\"; VAL=\"$3\"\n    RESULT=$(curl -sf -X POST \"$MCP\" \\\n        -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n        -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\\n        -H \"User-Agent: op-dbus/1.0\" \\\n        -d \"{\\\"jsonrpc\\\":\\\"2.0\\\",\\\"id\\\":1,\\\"method\\\":\\\"tools/call\\\",\\\"params\\\":{\\\"name\\\":\\\"cognitive_memory\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":{\\\"operation\\\":\\\"store\\\",\\\"namespace\\\":\\\"$NS\\\",\\\"key\\\":\\\"$KEY\\\",\\\"value\\\":$VAL}}}\" 2>&1) \\\n        && echo \"    ok: $NS/$KEY\" \\\n        || echo \"    WARN: could not write $NS/$KEY (cognitive-mcp may be unreachable)\"\n}\n\nNOW=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\n\n# Identity — cryptographic + hardware keys in CozoDB\nremember \"container:${CONTAINER_ID}:identity\" \"wireguard_pubkey\" \\\n    \"\\\"$PEER_PUBKEY\\\"\"\nremember \"container:${CONTAINER_ID}:identity\" \"mcp_token\" \\\n    \"\\\"$TOKEN\\\"\"\nif [ -n \"$MAC_ADDR\" ]; then\n    remember \"container:${CONTAINER_ID}:identity\" \"mac_address\" \\\n        \"\\\"$MAC_ADDR\\\"\"\nfi\nif [ -n \"$PSK\" ]; then\n    remember \"container:${CONTAINER_ID}:identity\" \"psk\" \\\n        \"\\\"$PSK\\\"\"\nfi\n\n# Email: store ONLY when GhostBridge is disabled.\n# GhostBridge users route through the privacy layer — email must not leak into CozoDB.\nif [ -n \"$EMAIL\" ] && [ \"$GHOSTBRIDGE\" = \"false\" ]; Implements the pipeline defined in\n//! `.kiro/specs/schemars-to-reflection-plugin-pipeline/` and the\n//! schema-coupled-plugin-blob-reflection whitepaper:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! Rust state/input/output structs (#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)])\n//!   -> schemars JSON Schema 2020-12\n//!   -> adapter::plugin_schema_from_json\n//!   -> PluginSchema                      <- SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH\n//!   -> blob::blobify\n//!   -> PluginObjectBlob                  <- sealed projection: schema + metadata\n//!        schema_json + schema_hash\n//!        D-Bus identity (/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>)\n//!        gRPC identity + FileDescriptorSet (typed, per-method)\n//!        method manifest (subid, capability, side_effect, idempotent)\n//!   -> catalog::ActiveReflectionCatalog  <- /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<id>.<hash>.blob\n//!   -> btrfs::seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image <- btrfs filesystem in the blob artifact\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Non-negotiable rules carried over from the whitepaper:\n//! 1. `PluginSchema` is the source of truth. The blob is a frozen projection,\n//!    never a second source.\n//! 2. The plugin owns its schema; schemars is the derivation tool, not the\n//!    published contract.\n//! 3. Blobs are per-object artifacts (one plugin, one blob, one schema hash),\n//!    replacing the monolithic `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` runtime shape.\n//! 4. Reflection advertises only active blobs; descriptors are synthesized\n//!    from `MethodDecl.args/returns` — no phantom services.\n//! 5. Zero-copy: a sealed blob is a sectioned byte image; `BlobRef` hands out\n//!    borrowed slices (schema JSON, manifest, descriptor bytes) without\n//!    re-parsing or re-allocating on the read path.\n//!\n//! Divergences from the full workspace (documented, deliberate):\n//! - `PluginSchema` here is a faithful but reduced port of\n//!   `op-state-store::plugin_schema` (this repo does not contain that crate).\n//!   Values use `serde_json::Value` instead of `simd_json::OwnedValue`.\n//! - Descriptor bytes are hand-encoded protobuf (`descriptor.rs`) instead of\n//!   prost — keeps the crate dependency-free per NFR-3's spirit.\n\npub mod adapter;\npub mod blob;\npub mod btrfs;\npub mod catalog;\npub mod demo;\npub mod descriptor;\npub mod identity;\npub mod schema;\npub mod subid;\n\npub use adapter::{\n    apply_state_defaults, method_decl_from_schemars_with_output, plugin_schema_from_json,\n    schema_diffs, AckOutput, EmptyInput,\n};\npub use blob::{\n    blobify, blobify_with_identity, BlobManifest, BlobRef, DbusIdentity, GrpcIdentity,\n    PluginObjectBlob,\n};\npub use catalog::ActiveReflectionCatalog;\npub use identity::{BlobIdentity, WgKeypair};\npub use schema::{Constraint, FieldSchema, FieldType, MethodDecl, PluginSchema, SideEffect};\npub use subid::validate_subid;\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f2a89-293b-7b21-bb3a-ee33de57f337"}}}

crate::blob::{BlobManifest, BlobRef, PluginObjectBlob};\nuse crate::descriptor;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\npub const DEFAULT_SHM_DIR: &str =
